VERDICT: NEEDS_IMPROVEMENT

FINDINGS:
- [HIGH] app/api/analyze/route.ts:800 - Research prompt tells the model "ALL SUBMITTED URLS TO CHECK VIA TOOL", but no tools exist (comment at 842-844 confirms googleSearch/urlContext are deliberately skipped). The model is instructed to perform a check it cannot perform, inviting fabricated "checked" claims that contradict the anti-hallucination rules at 809-813. Remove the "CHECK VIA TOOL" line and state explicitly that all data is provided inline and no web search is available.
- [HIGH] app/api/analyze/route.ts:862-863,1146 — If both Gemini and Groq fail in Pass 1, researchText becomes the sentinel "All AI providers failed...", yet Pass 2 still runs and the user is charged for a report synthesized from a failure string; data_quality can even read "full" when a transcript existed. Throw + refundEntitlement + return 502 when researchText equals the failure sentinel instead of proceeding.
- [HIGH] app/api/analyze/route.ts:1125-1131 (and prompt template at 897) — Synthesized fallback competitor entries claim "Checked across search and social platforms: No sponsorship deals..." while verification_status is "not_verifiable" — an assertion of a check that never happened (no search tool exists). Reword to "No evidence found in the provided data" to avoid fabricated verification claims.
- [MEDIUM] app/api/analyze/route.ts:73 — 15s per-call timeout × up to 3 models × 2 attempts per pass × 2 passes ≈ 90s worst case, leaving <30s for the Groq fallback, which has no timeout (see below); combined worst case exceeds the 120s maxDuration (line 11) and will 504 on the platform. Reduce per-call timeout or bound total pass time.
- [MEDIUM] app/api/analyze/route.ts:182-189 — Groq fallback fetch has no AbortController/timeout; a hung Groq request hangs the entire route until the platform 120s cap. Add an AbortController with a ~15-20s timeout mirroring the Gemini path.
- [MEDIUM] app/api/analyze/route.ts:1038-1048 — No retry on JSON parse failure: a single malformed synthesis response refunds the credit and returns 502. Add one retry with a repair prompt ("fix the JSON, return only valid JSON") before refunding.
- [MEDIUM] app/api/analyze/route.ts:946-947 vs 903 — responseSchema audience_insights.required omits toxic_recurring_themes and comment_sentiment_summary even though the prompt mandates them, and the runtime check (1052-1063) doesn't verify them either; downstream UI can receive undefined fields. Add both to schema required and to hasRequiredFields.
- [MEDIUM] app/api/analyze/route.ts:1062-1063 — final_verdict.recommendation is validated only as a non-empty string, not against the allowed set ("Sponsor"/"Proceed with Caution"/"Blacklist"); the schema (996) uses a description, not Type.ENUM. Enforce the enum in responseSchema and at runtime.
- [MEDIUM] app/api/analyze/route.ts:890-891,1074-1079 — brand_safety_score has no scoring rubric (single unanchored number, silently clamped to 0-100, NaN→50, null→0), so the most decision-critical output is the least constrained; a hallucinated score also drives the cache-guard overwrite decision at 1193. Add an explicit rubric (start at 100, deduct per verified red-flag category/severity) and require score↔risk_level consistency.
- [MEDIUM] app/api/analyze/route.ts:47-51 — Fallback model names "gemini-3.6-flash"/"gemini-3.5-flash"/"gemini-3.1-flash-lite" are unverifiable; if any don't exist, every Gemini call 404s and the pipeline silently degrades to Groq (or fails if GROQ_API_KEY is unset). Verify the names against the live API and log a hard error when all models fail rather than silently degrading.
- [MEDIUM] app/api/analyze/route.ts:803-804,837 — Prompt-injection defense is a single line buried in the checklist and the transcript/comments are embedded without delimiters; Pass 2 (870-871) embeds researchText with no "treat as data, not instructions" instruction, enabling second-order injection via a malicious transcript that poisons Pass 1 output. Wrap untrusted data in explicit delimiters (e.g., <untrusted_data>...</untrusted_data>) and add the same data-not-instructions rule to the synthesis prompt.
- [LOW] app/api/analyze/route.ts:851 — Gemini returning empty text yields the sentinel "No research findings generated." which flows into Pass 2 and still charges the user; treat empty research as a failure path (refund + 502) or mark data_quality "limited".
- [LOW] app/api/analyze/route.ts:910-1026 — No maxOutputTokens set on either pass; unbounded generation increases latency/cost and Pass 2 embeds researchText untruncated. Set maxOutputTokens (e.g., 4096 for Pass 2) and cap researchText length before embedding.
- [LOW] app/api/analyze/route.ts:139-148 — cleanJsonText strips only a single fence; trailing prose after the closing fence or a leading BOM still breaks JSON.parse. Strip all fences and trim to the first balanced JSON object.

# SafeSponsor AI — Security Audit

**VERDICT: FAIL**

**FINDINGS:**

- **[CRITICAL] app/api/webhook/route.ts:229-287** — Subscription revocation events are routed into the *grant* branch. `subscription.cancelled`/`subscription.expired`/`refund.succeeded` (with subscription context) force `plan="subscription"` (line 108-114), so the revocation branch `if (isRevocationEvent && (plan === "single" || plan === "channel"))` (line 229) is skipped, and `else if (plan === "subscription")` (line 246) executes the grant path: `tx.set(userRef, { ...entitlementUpdate, hasSubscription: true, subscription: { status: "active", expiresAt } }, { merge: true })` (line 279-286) — overriding the `hasSubscription: false` set at line 194. For an expired/cancelled sub with no valid future expiry, `baseMs = now` and `expiresAt = now + 1 month` (line 274-276): the user is **re-granted a free month**. Revocation never revokes. Fix: handle `isRevocationEvent` for ALL plans before the grant branch (e.g., `if (isRevocationEvent) { ...revoke... } else if (plan === "subscription") { ...grant... }`).

- **[MEDIUM] app/api/clear-cache/route.ts:18-27** — Any authenticated user can delete ANY `global_audits` entry by target_key (no admin/role check, no App Check, no ownership). Shared-cache DoS / cache-poisoning-by-deletion. Line 30 also returns raw `error.message` to the client (info disclosure). Fix: restrict to admin role (check `userData.role === "admin"` server-side) and return a generic error message.

- **[MEDIUM] app/api/analyze/route.ts:1167-1226** — Shared-cache poisoning: when no fresh `global_audits` entry exists (or it is stale >7 days), any user's report is written to the shared cache. A malicious user can prompt-inject the model via user-controlled `target`/`brand_name`/`competitor_brands` (injected at lines 792-838) to force a favorable report (score 100) for a bad creator, poisoning the cache for all free users for 7 days. The anti-injection instruction (line 836-837) is advisory only, and the cache guard (line 1197) only protects *existing fresh* entries. Fix: require a paid/subscribed user to write the global cache, or add a second independent verification pass before caching.

- **[MEDIUM] lib/firebase-admin.ts:33-58 + .env.example:34-36** — App Check is a no-op in production by default: `ENFORCE_APP_CHECK=false` makes `verifyAppCheckHeader` return `{valid:true}` for missing/invalid tokens (lines 39-45, 52-56). The App Check gates on analyze/checkout (analyze:245, checkout:16) provide zero protection under the shipped config. Fix: enforce App Check in production (or remove the false sense of security and rely solely on ID-token auth).

- **[MEDIUM] app/api/verify-payment/route.ts:30-93** — No App Check, no rate limiting, and the subscription grant (lines 83-91) sets `expiresAt = now + 1 month` without verifying the payment's actual billing period or refund status. The `lastPaymentId` check (line 66) and the write (line 93) are non-atomic — two concurrent calls can both pass the check (double-grant race). Fix: wrap the check+grant in a Firestore transaction and validate the payment's period/amount server-side.

- **[MEDIUM] next.config.ts:27** — CSP uses `script-src 'self' 'unsafe-inline'`; `'unsafe-inline'` defeats the primary XSS defense of CSP. `connect-src` also allows broad `wss:`. Fix: drop `'unsafe-inline'` (use nonces/hashes for the two inline scripts in layout.tsx) and tighten `connect-src`/`img-src` to explicit origins.

- **[LOW] app/api/webhook/route.ts:90-96** — Logs webhook signature prefix (30 chars) and headers to stdout; signature material should never be logged. Fix: log only `webhook-id` and event type.

- **[LOW] app/api/save-dossier/route.ts:14** — `request.json()` with no size cap; unbounded body can exhaust memory. Fix: enforce a 1MB limit like the other routes.

- **[LOW] app/api/webhook/route.ts:147-148** — `processed_webhooks` idempotency records accumulate forever (no TTL); unbounded collection growth. Fix: set a Firestore TTL policy on the collection.

- **[LOW] app/api/analyze/route.ts:1193-1197** — Cache-guard logic is inverted vs. its comment: it *skips* overwriting when the incoming report is materially MORE favorable (`newScore > oldScore + 15`), so a genuinely better report never replaces a stale conservative one, while a worse report with a lower risk weight can still overwrite. Not exploitable, but the anti-poisoning intent is only partially achieved.

**Verified clean:** No SSRF (all server fetches target fixed YouTube/Groq/Dodo endpoints with regex-validated IDs; `additional_urls` are never fetched — analyze:561, 674-703). No `eval`/`new Function`. `dangerouslySetInnerHTML` only in layout.tsx with static content (theme script, JSON-LD). No client-exposed `process.env` secrets (only `NEXT_PUBLIC_RECAPTCHA_SITE_KEY`). `.env.local` is gitignored; only `.env.example` (placeholders) and `firebase-applet-config.json` (public Firebase keys) are tracked. Firestore rules are sound: default deny, owner-only user reads, sensitive-field write protection (`isNotTouchingSensitiveFields`), history write denied to clients, `global_audits` read-only for clients. Webhook signature verification (standardwebhooks) + transactional idempotency + timestamp replay window are correctly implemented. Auth is consistently enforced via `verifyAuthHeader` on all 8 routes; no IDOR on user-scoped routes (check-credits, save-dossier, cancel-subscription, verify-payment all use the authenticated `uid`).

# SafeSponsor AI — Performance Audit

**Scope reviewed:** 8 API routes, dashboard/login/landing pages, Navbar, AuthProvider, seeded_audits, next.config.ts, layout.tsx. Live measurements taken against https://safe-sponsor-ai.vercel.app (TTFB + chunk sizes). Read-only; no files modified.

**VERDICT: CONCERNS**

The architecture is sound (cache-first analyze path, transactional entitlements, idempotent webhooks), but there are three structural latency/amplification problems: the analyze pipeline's worst-case budget exceeds its own `maxDuration`, the dashboard streams unbounded history + polls credits every 10s, and verify-payment lists the entire account payment history per call.

**FINDINGS**

- [HIGH] app/api/analyze/route.ts:47-102 — Gemini fallback chain (3 models × 2 attempts × 15s timeout + 2s/4s backoff) can consume ~108s per pass, ×2 passes, while `maxDuration=120` (line 11) is silently clamped to 60s on Vercel Hobby — realistic rate-limited audits 504 mid-flight. Impact: core feature times out; credits consumed then refunded inconsistently. Fix: lower per-call timeout, abort on first success, cap fallback to 1 model + Groq, or move to a background job with polling.
- [HIGH] app/api/analyze/route.ts:674-708 — `resolvedUrls` (up to 6 URLs for channel audits) processed in a strict sequential `for` loop, each URL doing transcript fetch then comments fetch serially; channel resolution (lines 587-645) is itself 3 sequential YouTube API calls. Impact: 30-60s+ of pure network latency before any AI call; channel audits routinely approach the 60s cap. Fix: `Promise.all` with bounded concurrency for transcript+comments per URL, and parallelize channels→search→videos.
- [HIGH] app/api/verify-payment/route.ts:35 — `dodo.payments.list({ status: "succeeded" })` with no date/uid filter fetches the account's entire succeeded-payment history on every checkout return; grows unboundedly with account volume. Impact: slow responses, large payloads, 502 risk as history grows. Fix: filter by `created_at` range or metadata.uid server-side, add `limit`.
- [HIGH] app/dashboard/page.tsx:215-218 — history `onSnapshot` with `orderBy("createdAt","desc")` and **no limit**; every dossier (full JSON incl. transcripts) is streamed to the client on every snapshot and re-streamed after each new audit. Impact: unbounded Firestore reads + client memory/parse cost as history grows. Fix: `.limit(50)` + pagination; keep only summary fields in the list query.
- [MEDIUM] app/api/analyze/route.ts:393 + 491 — user doc read twice per request: once at line 393 for the cache-skip decision, again inside the quota transaction. Impact: 2 reads/request on the hot path. Fix: fold the cache-skip check into the transaction result or reuse the snapshot.
- [MEDIUM] app/dashboard/page.tsx:270 — credits polled via `setInterval(fetchCredits, 10000)` → 6 Firestore reads/min per open tab, forever, even when idle. Impact: read amplification × concurrent tabs. Fix: poll on visibilitychange/focus only, or subscribe to the user doc via onSnapshot.
- [MEDIUM] Bundle: dashboard first load ≈ **900KB gzipped** across 15 async chunks (measured: cc44e60b=216KB, 255=173KB, 1770a7a7=167KB, 836=130KB, a36bde72=87KB, dashboard/page=98KB) — firebase auth+firestore, 40+ lucide icons, and motion/react all eager in one 3011-line client component. Impact: slow first paint/hydration on the primary app screen. Fix: lazy-load the dossier viewer, drop motion/react from dashboard, verify icon tree-shaking.
- [MEDIUM] app/api/analyze/route.ts:72-86 — the 15s timeout rejects the promise but never aborts the underlying Gemini request; the fallback proceeds to the next model while the orphaned call keeps running. Impact: concurrent in-flight Gemini calls, wasted quota, unpredictable wall-clock. Fix: `AbortController` wired to the timeout.
- [MEDIUM] app/dashboard/page.tsx:523-606 — batch queue runs audits strictly sequentially in a `for` loop; 20 items × 60-120s each = 20-40 min with the tab open, no server-side queue or resume. Impact: tab-close loses the whole batch; poor UX at scale. Fix: server-side job queue or at least concurrency-2 with persisted progress.
- [LOW] app/api/verify-payment/route.ts:96-103 — post-write `userRef.get()` verification read exists only for logging. Impact: 1 redundant Firestore read per grant. Fix: drop it.
- [LOW] app/page.tsx:245 — marketing claims "60-Second Executive Dossier Turnaround" while the pipeline can take 60-120s+ (see finding 1). Impact: expectation mismatch, support load. Fix: align copy or the pipeline.
- [LOW] app/api/analyze/route.ts:407 — global cache is skipped for all paid users (`!isPaidUser`), so every Pro audit pays full latency + AI cost even for repeat targets. Impact: cost/latency for subscribers. Fix: allow cache hits for subscribed users with a freshness window, or make force_refresh explicit.
- [INFO] app/api/analyze/route.ts:57 — `getAI()` constructs a new GoogleGenAI client per attempt; hoist to module scope. Impact: negligible allocation churn.

**Live measurements:** home/login/dashboard TTFB 1.0-1.3s (cold SSR, HTML 14-15KB — fine); the bottleneck is client JS execution (~900KB gzipped), not server HTML.

**What was checked and is OK:** webhook idempotency + entitlement transactions (bounded, non-user-facing); checkout (single Dodo call); cancel-subscription (single call + write); save-dossier/clear-cache/check-credits (single-doc ops); seeded_audits is server-only (no client bundle impact); no missing `Cache-Control` issues on auth'd routes; no N+1 Firestore loops in the payment routes.
